frozen_note: Written and committed before any outcome of protocol v1 (mover-early-entry-v1-20260924) or of this protocol was computed. It reuses v1's collections, definitions (rules.py), cost table and statistics, and v1's deviations D1-D3 and clarifications C1-C23 apply unless restated here.
prior_exposure_disclosed: Before this freeze the author had seen v1's development cost table (half-spreads about 20-75 bps per side), the counts of fired development entries (24,127 under v1's loosest rule), the D3 finding that 19% of pre-market-active candidate days trade above their regular-session high before the open, and the research package's chapter headlines and Wave H summary. No post-entry return of any rule has been computed.
question: Do entries earlier than v1's fixed clock times, the common follow-up setups on mover days, or pre-positioning at the previous close select US-equity symbol-days with positive returns net of realistic costs, and how much of each degree of eventual move do they capture?
user_scope: 2026-09-24 user instructions: pre-position or enter extreme movers at an early stage with auto leverage; strategies end to end on historical data, simulation and paper; follow-up strategies; use the Alpaca Elite data rate. Leverage stays a preregistered schedule; deterministic risk stays in code.

inputs.intraday: v1's candidate list plus the D3 pre-market supplement and their asof 2026-09-21 collections (bars 04:00-20:00, auctions, news)
inputs.daily: the broad-universe daily dataset (sha256 f7584f24519367e03e0a4ac0fc57f9b410c047991b001bb0259ebdfc09b31105): regular-session bars; close = official close on 92% of sampled days (v1 D3)
inputs.cost_table: v1's quote-measured development cost table, as committed for v1 (its sha256 is recorded in v1's results)

E_first_cross.idea: earliest-stage entry: enter at the first minute a mover condition becomes true, instead of at a fixed clock time
E_first_cross.rule: for window W and thresholds (G, V): the first 1-minute bar k starting in W such that, using bars starting before bar k's start, gain_at >= G, dollar_volume_at >= V and price_at >= $1; enter at bar k's open (a bar starting at or after 09:30 when k is the first regular-session bar; in the pre-market, bar k must start before 09:30)
E_first_cross.completeness: every G >= 0.20 condition holds only on a v1 candidate or D3 supplement day (the superset argument of v1 and D3)
E_first_cross.live_mapping: a full-market snapshot scan every 10 s (about 20 snapshot requests per scan, ~120 per minute at 8,000 symbols) plus minute bars for the prefiltered names; well inside the Elite 10,000-per-minute data limit

F_followup_setups.idea: common practitioner setups on a mover day, entered after the open
F_followup_setups.universe: symbol-days whose official open is at least 1.20 x ref (gap-up movers; ref as v1), price >= $1, dollar volume before 09:30 >= $250,000

setups.F1_orb5: opening-range breakout: range = high and low of bars starting 09:30-09:34; enter at the open of the first bar starting 09:35-10:59 whose high exceeds the range high, at max(bar open, range high); initial stop = range low
setups.F2_orb15: as F1 with the 09:30-09:44 range and entries 09:45-10:59
setups.F3_premarket_high_break: enter at max(bar open, pre-market high) in the first bar starting 09:30-10:59 whose high exceeds the high of bars starting 04:00-09:29; initial stop = the official open x 0.90
setups.F4_vwap_reclaim: session VWAP from 04:00 (vwap x volume / volume, cumulative); after the first bar starting at or after 09:35 that closes below VWAP, enter at the open of the next bar after a bar that closes back above VWAP, starting before 11:00; initial stop = the lowest low since 09:30

exits.Y2_stop_or_close: the setup's initial stop (fill min(stop, bar open) for gaps), else the official close
exits.Y3_stop_trail: the initial stop until the running high reaches 1.10 x entry, then a 10% trail off the running high through the previous bar, else the official close
exits.Y4_stop_2r: the initial stop, or a target of entry + 2 x (entry - stop) (the stop is assumed first in a bar reaching both), else the official close

F_followup_setups.costs: v1 per-side costs by bucket; entries are bar fills (1.25 x half-spread), exits as v1

P_preposition.idea: pre-position at the previous session's official close in names likely to be the next session's extreme movers, and day-2 continuation
P_preposition.universe: every daily-dataset symbol-day (less likely warrants, units and rights) with close >= $1 and dollar volume >= $1,000,000 on the entry day d

scores.S1_day2_runner: day d's close / day d-1's close - 1 >= 0.30 and close >= 0.90 x day d's high
scores.S2_volume_breakout: day d's volume >= 5 x the median volume of days d-20..d-1, close >= the 20-day high, and day d's return >= +10%
scores.S3_compression_expansion: day d's range is the narrowest of the last 7 days (NR7) and its volume >= 3 x the 20-day median
scores.S4_gap_and_hold: day d's open >= 1.20 x day d-1's close and day d's close >= day d's open

P_preposition.ranking: within a score's qualifying set, rank by day d's dollar volume descending, then symbol; at most 5 entries per session
P_preposition.entry: day d's daily-bar close as the proxy for the official close (the closing auction); v1 D3 measured the daily close equal to the official closing print on 92% of sampled days

exits.Z1_next_open: day d+1's daily-bar open as the proxy for the official open (78% agreement in v1 D3)
exits.Z3_open_stop_close: exit at day d+1's open if it is below day d's close x 0.95, else at day d+1's close

P_preposition.costs: each auction side pays 0.5 x the v1 half-spread of its bucket (09:30-10:00 for the open, 10:00-16:00 for the close) with the tier of that side's price and day d's dollar volume; fees as v1
P_preposition.capture: the share of day d+1's degree-tier movers (v1 tiers on day d+1's close over day d's close) that a score selected, against the tier's base rate among the universe
P_preposition.overnight: held overnight; leverage capped at 2 (Reg T) and the drawdown factor as v1
P_preposition.proxy_note: all P prices come from the daily dataset for every symbol; auction prints are fetched only for traded names in the paper step

definitions_shared: ref, split factor, tiers, the halt flag, fills with gaps (min(level, bar open) for stops; max(level, bar open) for breakout entries), windows ending at the last bar starting before 16:00, fees and C6/C7 net-return formulas all as v1
statistics: as v1: circular session block bootstrap (5-session blocks, B = 20,000; seed = the first 8 bytes of sha256('mover-followup-v2-20260924'), big-endian); one-sided p = (1 + #{mean_b <= 0}) / (B + 1); quantised sums; sensitivities BY, two-way clustering

selection_and_pass_criteria.families_separately: each family (E, F, P) is its own family for multiple testing
selection_and_pass_criteria.development: a rule-exit passes with >= 200 trades (P: >= 100) and p <= 0.05 on the mean net return
selection_and_pass_criteria.validation: confirmed with >= 100 trades (P: >= 50), BH-adjusted p <= 0.10 across the family's development passes, and positive winsorised, without-top-5-sessions and per-session means
selection_and_pass_criteria.holdout: at most 3 validated rule-exits per family, lowest validation p; Holm-adjusted p <= 0.05 with >= 50 trades (P: >= 30); holdout sessions are not read before this step
selection_and_pass_criteria.no_pass: if nothing passes, that is the result for that family

portfolio_and_leverage: as v1 (start $100,000; 5 positions; rungs 1/2/4 x regime x drawdown factors, cooldown, capacity 1% of the decision-time dollar volume and 10% of the entry bar's; sub-$5 names at 1x), with family P capped at 2x overnight
paper_and_sim: Each validated rule-exit gets (1) a simulation run through the adaptive engine's synthetic path with the same fills, and (2) a paper trial through the engine's mover mode on an account no other user trades during the trial. Family E maps to a continuous scanner; F to regular-hours entries; P to a closing-auction entry (MOC/LOC before the broker cutoff) and an opening or closing exit. A family with no validated rule-exit gets a labelled mechanics-only trial of its most-traded development rule-exit.
reproduction: deterministic given the inputs; re-runs must reproduce the result files byte for byte
overturn: a byte-level reproduction failure, or an independent quote sample showing the cost table off by more than 2x, overturns any headline result
